title.en: Fourier harmonic synthesis with complex phasors

summary: Connect a finite bank of odd harmonics to a square-wave approximation and expose truncation near jumps.
objective: Change harmonic count and inspect which rotating component contributes to the instantaneous sum.
intent_signals: Change harmonic count and inspect which rotating component contributes to the instantaneous sum.
Connect a finite bank of odd harmonics to a square-wave approximation and expose truncation near jumps.
example_prompts: Build an explorable fourier harmonic synthesis with complex phasors. Change harmonic count and inspect which rotating component contributes to the instantaneous sum.

entities.name: Phasor assembly
entities.guidance: Draw tip-to-tail arrows in an equal-scale real/imaginary plane, one for each retained odd harmonic; arrow k has length4/(pi*(2k+1)). Put frequency and coefficient labels on selectable parts.

entities.name: Complex time trace
entities.guidance: Construct a sampled curve (t, Re S_N(t), Im S_N(t)), with all three axes labeled; the third dimension encodes the second complex component, not decorative depth. Link its imaginary projection to a conventional t-versus-amplitude panel.

entities.name: Target and jump inspection
entities.guidance: Overlay the target sign(sin t) away from integer multiples of pi. Mark jumps with open endpoints and the midpoint value0 as the series convention; do not connect target jumps with sloped interpolation.

state_contract.model: Use dimensionless phase t in[0,2pi] and integer1<=N<=32. S_N(t)=sum(k=0..N-1)4*exp(i*(2k+1)*t)/(pi*(2k+1)); f_N=Im S_N. The square-wave preset fixes these coefficients. Sampling for display uses M>=16*(2N-1) intervals per period plus a doubling comparison; this is an authored resolution rule, not a universal error bound.
state_contract.authority: N, phase, sample count and preset own every arrow and trace. A camera orbit or hidden component does not change its numerical contribution; use a separately labeled mute action to alter the sum.
actions: Select a harmonic and reveal its coefficient, frequency and component trace.
Change N and rebuild the finite sum; retain phase.
Scrub or play phase, pause without phase drift, and zoom around a jump.
Optional coefficient editing enters a labeled custom finite-series mode; square-wave convergence labels are then disabled.
Reset N, phase, sample count and preset.

invariants: Tip-to-tail endpoint equals the independently summed real/imaginary components within a declared floating-point tolerance.
For the square preset f_N(0)=f_N(pi)=0 analytically; at t+pi the imaginary sum changes sign.
Increasing N does not justify a uniform-error-to-zero claim across a discontinuity. Check sampled extrema with doubled resolution before quoting a displayed peak.
motion_guidance: Derive each phasor angle from harmonic number times the same phase; never give it an independent clock.
A cursor projects the complex trace into its imaginary waveform. The connecting segments interpolate displayed samples, not the infinite Fourier series.
known_limits: This is a finite authored synthesis bank, not a measured spectrum, FFT, audio reconstruction guarantee or band-unlimited sampler.
Gibbs overshoot narrows toward a jump as N grows but its limiting relative height does not vanish; avoid claiming every finite N has exactly the asymptotic overshoot.
Authored recipe and prospective checks only; no runtime artifact or rendered result has been observed.

claims.statement: The period-2pi odd square wave has Fourier series (4/pi) sum over positive odd n of sin(nt)/n. Its partial sums exhibit Gibbs overshoot near jumps; increasing the number of terms does not eliminate the limiting overshoot height.
claims.scope: Odd square-wave Fourier series and its jump behavior; not arbitrary sampled-signal reconstruction.

source_refs.locator: 22.6.1 square-wave partial sums and 22.6.2 Gibbs phenomenon, PDF page index 202; Eq.34 at index206

object_craft.family: Fourier harmonic synthesis with complex phasors
object_craft.structure: Keep phasor pivots, vector tips, projection guides and the time-trace frame separately selectable. Rescaling a view must not silently alter coefficient lengths relative to one another.
object_craft.material: Use independent line weights, shapes and labels for mathematical roles. Color and surface finish are presentation choices; do not infer material physics from them.

creative_affordances: A mechanical-looking harmonic bank, clean signal lab or playful ribbon trace can express the same sum; no particular shader or hardware is required.

physical_contract.scope: Derived mathematical geometry and authored inspection; no contact dynamics or calibrated physical artifact.
